title_en: Zhao Chen — case of being defrauded due to negligence in signing a contract
keywords_en: Criminal; Crime of Dereliction of Duty in Signing and Performing Contracts Resulting in Fraud; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Shanghai; Natural Person; Legal Person; Criminal Law; Whether Constituting the Crime of Dereliction of Duty in Signing and Performing Contracts Resulting in Fraud; Whether the Defendant Was Grossly Irresponsible; Causal Relationship between the Loss and the Defendant's Conduct; State-owned Enterprise; Signing a Contract; Being Defrauded; Loan; Dereliction of Duty
full_text_en:
Zhao Chen Sentenced for Dereliction of Duty in Contract Signing Resulting in Fraud

Prosecutorial Authority: Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate.

Defendant: Zhao Chen, male, 51 years old, former General Manager of Shanghai County Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation and concurrently General Manager of Shanghai Hongkang Real Estate Corporation, released on bail pending trial by the Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate on May 20, 1997, on suspicion of dereliction of duty.

Defense Counsel: Zhang Shengzhong, lawyer of Shanghai Dagong Law Firm.

Defense Counsel: Dai Hongru, lawyer of Shanghai Huanzhong Law Firm.

The defendant Zhao Chen was prosecuted by the Shanghai Minhang District People's Procuratorate before the Shanghai Minhang District People's Court on charges of dereliction of duty in contract signing resulting in fraud.

The indictment alleged: The defendant Zhao Chen, as a directly responsible supervisor of a state-owned enterprise, trusted the introduction of a friend and assigned subordinates to sign a procurement and sales contract. In particular, when a subordinate reminded him that he should verify the authenticity of the other party's business, he still refused to accept that opinion. Due to Zhao Chen's grave irresponsibility, public funds of the unit were defrauded, causing significant losses to state interests. His conduct has constituted the crime of being defrauded due to dereliction of duty in signing contracts, and a conviction and punishment according to law were requested.

Zhao Chen argued: The business charged in the indictment was introduced by me to Shen Caixing, manager of Shanghai Hongkang Building Materials Company (hereinafter referred to as Hongkang Building Materials). Because Hongkang Building Materials had no money, I agreed to lend them over RMB 1.5 million from Shanghai Hongkang Real Estate Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Hongkang Real Estate). Hongkang Building Materials is an independent legal entity. The success or failure of this business should be borne by Shen Caixing, the legal representative of Hongkang Building Materials, and has nothing to do with me.

The defense counsel's opinion was: The contract charged in the indictment was signed between Hongkang Building Materials and Shanghai Datong Technology Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Datong Company). A creditor-debtor relationship arose between Hongkang Building Materials and Datong Company as a result of this contract. Datong Company owed a debt to Hongkang Building Materials, which could have been recovered through legal channels, but because Hongkang Building Materials waived its right of recourse, huge losses were caused. Zhao Chen was not the directly responsible supervisor for signing this contract. There was no issue of grave irresponsibility, and the huge losses suffered were unrelated to him. Although Zhao Chen introduced this business, he did not obtain any personal gain from it. Therefore, Zhao Chen's conduct did not constitute a crime. The evidence for the crime charged in the indictment was insufficient, and the defendant should be acquitted.

After trial, the Shanghai Minhang District People's Court found:

Shanghai County Urban and Rural Construction Development Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Urban-Rural Corporation) was a state-owned enterprise subordinate to the former Shanghai County Construction Bureau. Hongkang Real Estate was a state-owned enterprise subordinate to the Red Cross Society of China. The two companies operated as "two signboards but one management team" but had no administrative or financial affiliation. Between September 1992 and February 1993, the defendant Zhao Chen served as the general manager and legal representative of both companies.

Hongkang Building Materials was a collectively-owned tertiary enterprise established by the trade union of Urban-Rural Corporation in December 1992. It had independent legal personality and independent financial accounting. Moon Veil Shop was an independent business unit under Urban-Rural Corporation without legal personality, holding a business special seal of Urban-Rural Corporation, with its finances uniformly managed by Urban-Rural Corporation but maintaining separate accounts. Shen Caixing, the trade union chairman of Urban-Rural Corporation, served as the manager and legal representative of Hongkang Building Materials, and concurrently as the person in charge of Moon Veil Shop.

On January 10, 1993, Yao Guanming and Hao Fengming, former cadres of the Shanghai County Labor Bureau, came to Urban-Rural Corporation and introduced a steel wire rod business to the defendant Zhao Chen. Zhao Chen believed that an introduction by a friend must be reliable and agreed to do this business without understanding the situation of the supplier, and assigned Shen Caixing to handle it specifically. Shen Caixing proposed to verify the supplier's situation before making a decision, but Zhao Chen ignored him. A few days later, Yao Guanming and Hao Fengming came to negotiate with Zhao Chen on the specifications, price, quantity, etc. of the steel wire rods. Zhao Chen called Shen Caixing to his office and introduced the negotiated situation to Shen Caixing. Shen Caixing proposed to see the delivery order, but Zhao Chen did not respond. On January 16, Hao Fengming again urged Zhao Chen to sign the contract and pay the货款. Zhao Chen asked Shen Caixing to draft the contract with Hao Fengming. Shen Caixing again proposed to see the delivery order before payment, but Zhao Chen still did not pay attention, said there was no problem, and made the final decision for Shen Caixing to pay. Shen Caixing said his department had no funds, and Zhao Chen asked him to first borrow from Hongkang Real Estate. Under these circumstances, Shen Caixing returned to his office with Hao Fengming and asked his subordinate Ding Jianhua to draft a contract for Urban-Rural Corporation to purchase 500 tons of steel wire rods from Shanghai Datong Technology Engineering Company (hereinafter referred to as Datong Company) with a total price of RMB 1.525 million. Shen Caixing also asked Ding Jianhua, following Zhao Chen's intention, to write a report in the name of Hongkang Building Materials to borrow RMB 1.525 million from Hongkang Real Estate. Zhao Chen instructed accountant Fu Jianliang to transfer RMB 1.525 million from Hongkang Real Estate into the account of Moon Veil Shop, and then Moon Veil Shop issued a transfer check of the same amount to Datong Company. Hao Fengming delivered the contract, which bore only the signature and seal of Urban-Rural Corporation, and the transfer check to the business department of Datong Company. After receiving the payment, the business department of Datong Company only delivered 75.6 tons of steel wire rods worth RMB 230,580, and used the remaining payment to repay debts and for squandering.

Further investigation revealed: Datong Company was a tertiary enterprise subordinate to the Science and Technology Commission of Yangpu District, Shanghai. Its business department was contracted out to Ge Haigen, an unemployed person. Because Ge Haigen did not operate lawfully during the contract period and accumulated heavy debts, Datong Company terminated the contracting agreement with Ge Haigen in December 1992 and revoked the business department. During the operation of the business department of Datong Company, it owed more than RMB 800,000 in货款 to Dongmin Industry and Trade Company. Due to the urgent debt recovery by Chen Baolin of Dongmin Industry and Trade Company and the revocation of the business department, Ge Haigen decided to adopt a "rob Peter to pay Paul" approach to repay debts, asking Chen Baolin to find a unit that needed to purchase steel, stating that the debt would be repaid once funds arrived. Chen Baolin told Hao Fengming about the information that Datong Company could supply steel wire rods, and Hao Fengming then introduced it to Zhao Chen. In fact, at the time Urban-Rural Corporation signed the contract, the business department of Datong Company no longer existed, and Ge Haigen had neither the qualifications to sign contracts nor the ability to perform them, but only intended to use this contract to defraud money to repay debts. Ge Haigen had already been sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment by the Shanghai Pudong New Area People's Court in March 1996 for the crime of fraud. The more than RMB 1.29 million货款 defrauded from Urban-Rural Corporation has been irrecoverable to date. Because Urban-Rural Corporation had consistently pursued this irrecoverable defrauded sum as a debt dispute, this fraudulent fact was not determined in Ge Haigen's criminal judgment.

The above facts are supported by the following evidence: 1. Certification of the defendant Zhao Chen's identity, position, and term of office; 2. Certification of the establishment of Hongkang Building Materials and the issuance of its business license as a legal person by the industry and commerce department; 3. The procurement and sales contract signed between Urban-Rural Corporation and Datong Company; 4. Written evidence of Hongkang Building Materials' loan from Hongkang Real Estate; 5. Bank deposit slip of RMB 1.525 million transferred from Hongkang Real Estate to the account of Urban-Rural Corporation; 6. Transfer check used by Urban-Rural Corporation to pay that amount to Datong Company; 7. Account records of Urban-Rural Corporation reflecting that the payment was made to Datong Company in the name of Moon Veil Shop; 8. Testimony of witness Hao Fengming stating, "Chen Baolin said Datong Company had steel wire rods to supply, and I introduced the business to Zhao Chen. Zhao assigned Shen Caixing to handle this business specifically. Shen questioned whether the supplier was reliable, and Zhao said it was reliable and no problem. Before payment, both Shen Caixing and Ding Jianhua proposed to first see the other party's delivery order, but Zhao did not pay attention and still made the final decision to pay"; 9. Testimony of witness Yao Guanming stating, "Before Urban-Rural Corporation signed the contract and made payment, I said to Zhao Chen that it would be best to pay after the other party delivered the goods. Zhao heard but did not respond. This business was decided by Zhao Chen, who then told Shen Caixing to operate"; 10. Testimony of witness Shen Caixing stating, "I repeatedly told Zhao Chen that this business was risky and that we should see the delivery order before paying, but Zhao repeatedly said the business introduced by a friend was absolutely reliable. I said there was no money, and Zhao said the money would be arranged by him. After payment, Datong Company only delivered 75.6 tons of steel wire rods, and thereafter no goods were seen and the debt was not recovered. To clarify responsibility, on June 23, 1993, I wrote 'An Explanation of the Process Before and After the Transaction of 500 Tons of Steel Wire Rods', and Zhao Chen signed 'The situation is true'"; 11. Testimony of witness Fu Jianliang stating, "Zhao Chen asked me to bring a check to his office. At that time, Shen Caixing said this business was not good to do and was very dangerous. Zhao said it must be done, and the money would be borrowed from Hongkang Real Estate. The deposit slip went into the account of Moon Veil Shop, but in fact it also entered the account of Urban-Rural Corporation. The check issued to Datong Company was from that account, not from the account of Hongkang Building Materials"; 12. Testimony of witness Ding Jianhua stating, "Shen Caixing did not want to do this business and made excuses by saying there was no money, but Zhao Chen instructed Shen to handle it, saying the money would be solved by him. So Shen asked me to draft the sales contract"; 13. Confession of Ge Haigen stating, "Because I was deep in debt, I wanted to cheat some money to repay debts. I discussed with my creditor Chen Baolin to find a client outside. Once the money was received, I would repay him. In fact, there was no steel. Later, the check was brought by Chen Baolin and a person named Hao. I delivered more than 200,000 yuan worth of steel, and the remaining money was used to repay debts and for consumption"; 14. Testimony of witness Zhang Lijuan, accountant of the business department of Datong Company, stating, "We did not have the goods for the contract signed with Urban-Rural Corporation. Later we obtained some goods, but only delivered more than 200,000 yuan worth. The money was used to repay debts and for other expenses"; 15. Testimony of witness Chen Baolin stating, "Datong Company owed me more than 800,000 yuan in货款. They asked me to find a company that wanted to buy steel, and once the money arrived in their account, they would repay my debt. I found Urban-Rural Corporation through Hao Fengming"; 16. Testimony of witness Zhou Caiqing, General Manager of Datong Company, stating, "Ge Haigen contracted the business department of Datong Company. Later, it was found that he did not operate lawfully, so in December 1992, a notice was issued to terminate the contract and the privately engraved seal of the business department was taken back"; 17. Written notice of termination of Ge Haigen's contracting agreement by Datong Company; 18. Receipt for the return of the official seal of the business department of Datong Company; 19. Receipts of Datong Company using the payment received from Urban-Rural Corporation to repay debts; 20. Criminal judgment sentencing Ge Haigen for the crime of fraud. The above evidence, after being examined in court, can corroborate each other and is sufficient to serve as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

The Shanghai Minhang District People's Court held:

During his tenure as the legal representative and general manager of Urban-Rural Corporation, a state-owned enterprise, the defendant Zhao Chen, trusting the introduction of a friend, failed to inquire or investigate the subject qualification, performance ability, and source of goods of the counterparty of the contract, and despite repeated reminders from subordinates, persisted in his own course and instructed subordinates to sign a procurement and sales contract with others, resulting in significant losses of nearly RMB 1.3 million in state property being defrauded. Under the law at that time, such conduct constituted the crime of dereliction of duty. According to Article 12 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, Zhao Chen shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Law.

Article 167 of the Criminal Law stipulates: "Where a directly responsible supervisor of a state-owned company, enterprise, or institution, in the process of signing or performing a contract, is defrauded due to grave irresponsibility, thereby causing significant losses to the interests of the state, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention; if particularly significant losses are caused to the interests of the state, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years and not more than seven years." The subject of this crime is a supervisor of a state-owned company, enterprise, or institution who can play a leading, decision-making, or commanding role in the signing and performance of contracts, not a person who merely engages in the work of signing or performing under orders. The defendant Zhao Chen, as a supervisor of a state-owned enterprise, played an obvious decision-making role in the process of signing the contract involved in this case, which meets the special requirement for the subject of this crime. Zhao Chen bore the responsibility of managing and operating state-owned assets. He should have known that the signing and performance of a contract carry certain risks and the possibility of being defrauded, and therefore he should have diligently performed the duty of examining the subject qualification and performance ability of the other party before signing the contract. Because a friend introduced the business, Zhao Chen lightly believed that the harmful consequences of being defrauded could be avoided. Driven by this negligent mentality, Zhao Chen abandoned his duties. Zhao Chen's subjective state of mind meets the requirement for the subjective aspect of this crime. Therefore, when the harmful result of nearly RMB 1.3 million in state property being defrauded occurred objectively, Zhao Chen's conduct indeed constituted the crime of being defrauded due to dereliction of duty in signing contracts.

Hongkang Building Materials was a legal person established by Urban-Rural Corporation, and its legal representative Shen Caixing was a subordinate of the defendant Zhao Chen. Shen Caixing only engaged in the specific work of signing the contract under the direction of Zhao Chen. The contract, in name, bore the seal of Urban-Rural Corporation, not Hongkang Building Materials; in essence, the transaction was decided by Zhao Chen, the legal representative of Urban-Rural Corporation, not related to Hongkang Building Materials. Zhao Chen's defense that the contract was signed by Shen Caixing on behalf of Hongkang Building Materials, and that Hongkang Building Materials was an independent legal person and Shen Caixing should be responsible for the contract, cannot be established. The facts prove that during the contract signing process, Shen Caixing repeatedly proposed to understand the true situation of the other party, but Zhao Chen did not accept this; when Shen Caixing again declined on the ground that his unit had no funds, Zhao Chen advocated borrowing from Hongkang Real Estate first. Therefore, the borrowing was by no means an initiative of Hongkang Building Materials, but a way of circulating funds decided by Zhao Chen for Urban-Rural Corporation to provide capital. Ge Haigen, in the name of Datong Company, claimed to sell steel wire rods only to defraud货款. After the fraud succeeded, the货款 was used to repay debts and for squandering. In relation to this货款, a relationship of Ge Haigen defrauding Urban-Rural Corporation was formed, not a creditor-debtor relationship between Hongkang Building Materials and Datong Company. The defense counsel's opinion that Hongkang Building Materials could have recovered the debt from Datong Company through legal channels, but because Hongkang Building Materials waived its right of recourse, huge losses were caused, is inconsistent with the facts and cannot be established. Zhao Chen's grave irresponsibility caused significant losses to state property, and his dereliction of duty has constituted a crime. The fact that Zhao Chen did not obtain any personal gain during the signing of this contract does not affect the constitution of the crime. The defense counsel's opinion that Zhao Chen's conduct does not constitute a crime is not adopted.

In summary, the facts charged in the indictment are clear, the evidence is sufficient and reliable, and the charges are established and should be confirmed. The defense counsel's opinions have been negated by the established facts and the reasons set forth above and are therefore not adopted. Although the defendant Zhao Chen once had vague understanding of his conduct, after trial he has recognized the harmfulness of his conduct, sincerely expressed his guilt, and requested lenient treatment. Considering Zhao Chen's criminal circumstances and attitude of repentance, the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 72 of the Criminal Law regarding probation may be applied to Zhao Chen. Accordingly, the Shanghai Minhang District People's Court adjudged:

The defendant Zhao Chen is convicted of the crime of being defrauded due to dereliction of duty in signing contracts and sentenced to two years' imprisonment with a two-year suspension.

After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Zhao Chen did not appeal, and the prosecutorial authority did not protest. The first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
